concepts.title: French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation' refers to.
questions.a: The 1789 French Revolution gave nationalism its first clear expression by transferring sovereignty from the monarch to the citizen body and inventing symbols, language and rituals of collective identity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation'.
questions.a: Revolutionary measures such as the tricolour flag, anthems, oaths and a centralised administrative system carried the national idea from France into the rest of Europe.

questions.q: Under which section is 'French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation (source: jess301.txt lines 113-165)

concepts.title: Napoleon's Administrative Reforms and the Civil Code

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Napoleon's Administrative Reforms and the Civil Code' refers to.
questions.a: Napoleon destroyed democracy in France yet rationalised administration in conquered lands through the Civil Code of 1804, which secured equality before the law, the right to property and simplified weights, currencies and taxes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Napoleon's Administrative Reforms and the Civil Code'.
questions.a: The Napoleonic Code removed privileges by birth and improved transport systems in Switzerland, Italy and Germany, letting some see him as a liberator while others saw an occupying force.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Napoleon's Administrative Reforms and the Civil Code' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation (source: jess301.txt lines 167-296)

concepts.title: Liberalism in Political and Economic Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Liberalism in Political and Economic Life' refers to.
questions.a: Liberalism stood for freedom of the individual, equality before the law and government by consent in politics, and for freedom of markets and abolition of state-imposed tariffs in economics, drawing support mainly from the educated middle classes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Liberalism in Political and Economic Life'.
questions.a: Prussia created the Zollverein customs union of 1834 that removed tariff barriers across most German states and became a nationalist economic engine, though universal suffrage stayed denied to women and the propertyless.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Liberalism in Political and Economic Life' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe (source: jess301.txt lines 346-405)

concepts.title: Vienna Congress of 1815 and the Conservative Order

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Vienna Congress of 1815 and the Conservative Order' refers to.
questions.a: After Napoleon's defeat in 1815, Britain, Russia, Prussia and Austria met at Vienna to restore monarchy and undo the changes he had carried, drawing a conservative settlement that redrew boundaries in favour of the great powers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Vienna Congress of 1815 and the Conservative Order'.
questions.a: The Bourbon dynasty returned to France, a German confederation of 39 states replaced the Napoleonic system, and Austria gained northern Italy while Russia took part of Poland.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Vienna Congress of 1815 and the Conservative Order' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe (source: jess301.txt lines 406-470)

concepts.title: Revolutions, Romantic Culture and the Greek War of Independence

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Revolutions, Romantic Culture and the Greek War of Independence' refers to.
questions.a: Uprisings in 1830 and 1848 challenged the conservative order, while Romanticism fed nationalism through folk songs, poetry and dances that gathered popular feelings, and Greece's war of independence from 1821 became a symbol of the age.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Revolutions, Romantic Culture and the Greek War of Independence'.
questions.a: Treaty of Constantinople in 1832 recognised Greece as an independent nation; poets and artists lauded Greece as the cradle of European civilisation and mobilised support from exiled Greeks.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Revolutions, Romantic Culture and the Greek War of Independence' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Revolutionaries (source: jess301.txt lines 470-560)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unification of Germany' refers to.
questions.a: Prussia's chief minister Otto von Bismarck built German unity through three wars with Denmark, Austria and France over seven years, and the Prussian king William I was proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles in January 1871.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unification of Germany'.
questions.a: The unification was carried by the army and bureaucracy rather than by the liberal Frankfurt parliament of 1848, whose dream of a nation built by the people failed.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Unification of Germany' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Unification of Germany (source: jess301.txt lines 830-970)

questions.q: How many volunteers joined garibaldi beyond the expedition of the thousand? Use the method 'Growth of Garibaldi's Red Shirts'. Work with: final_volunteers = 150, initial_volunteers = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of added_volunteers.
questions.a: 146 units

questions.q: Calculate the growth of the red shirts during the 1860 campaign. Use the method 'Growth of Garibaldi's Red Shirts'. Work with: final_volunteers = 400, initial_volunteers = 400. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of added_volunteers.
questions.a: 0 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Growth of Garibaldi's Red Shirts' refers to.
questions.a: Giuseppe Garibaldi sailed from Genoa in 1860 with a band of a thousand volunteers for South Italy, and fresh recruits swelled the force to about thirty thousand, so the added volunteers equal the final strength minus the initial expedition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Growth of Garibaldi's Red Shirts'.
questions.a: The Red Shirts took Naples and South Italy in the Expedition of the Thousand; in 1867 Garibaldi's march on Rome failed against French and Papal troops until 1870, when France recalled its garrison.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Growth of Garibaldi's Red Shirts', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: added_volunteers = final_volunteers - initial_volunteers

concepts.title: Unification of Italy and Its Architects

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unification of Italy and Its Architects' refers to.
questions.a: Italy's unity was forged by Mazzini's secret Young Italy, Count Cavour's diplomacy and alliance with France, and Garibaldi's armed expedition, so that Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed King of united Italy in 1861.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unification of Italy and Its Architects'.
questions.a: Italians of different regions spoke dialects and had not seen one another, and Mazzini believed nations were the natural units of mankind, making Italy a people's nation in the making.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Unification of Italy and Its Architects' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Unification of Italy (source: jess301.txt lines 1140-1230)

questions.q: Calculate the years between the french revolution and german unification. Use the method 'Years Between National Milestones'. Work with: earlier_year = 150, later_year = 2600. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of years_elapsed.
questions.a: 2450 years

questions.q: How many years passed between two nationalist events? Use the method 'Years Between National Milestones'. Work with: earlier_year = 25, later_year = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of years_elapsed.
questions.a: 125 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Years Between National Milestones' refers to.
questions.a: The span between two nationalist landmarks, such as the 1789 French Revolution and the 1871 proclamation of the German Empire, is found by subtracting the earlier year from the later year.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Years Between National Milestones'.
questions.a: Roughly eight decades separate the first clear expression of nationalism in France from the completed unification of Germany and Italy.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Years Between National Milestones', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: years_elapsed = later_year - earlier_year

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Strange Case of Britain' refers to.
questions.a: Britain became a nation not by a sudden revolution but by the long dominance of England over Scotland and Ireland, starting with the Act of Union of 1707 that created the United Kingdom of Great Britain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Strange Case of Britain'.
questions.a: Scottish Highlanders were barred from Gaelic and national dress, and after Wolfe Tone's failed 1798 revolt Ireland was forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom in 1801.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Strange Case of Britain' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Strange Case of Britain (source: jess301.txt lines 973-1025)

concepts.title: Visualising the Nation: Marianne and Germania

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Visualising the Nation: Marianne and Germania' refers to.
questions.a: Artists gave the abstract nation a concrete face by personifying it as a female figure: France was christened Marianne with the red cap, tricolour and cockade, while Germania wore a crown of oak leaves standing for heroism.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Visualising the Nation: Marianne and Germania'.
questions.a: Marianne images were stamped on coins and statues stood in public squares; Germania's banner hung in the Church of St Paul during the Frankfurt parliament of 1848.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Visualising the Nation: Marianne and Germania' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Visualising the Nation (source: jess301.txt lines 1060-1160)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nationalism, Imperialism and the Balkans' refers to.
questions.a: After 1871 the most serious nationalist tension gathered in the Balkans, where slavic peoples broke from Ottoman rule even as the great powers competed to extend their own influence, turning nationalism into imperialism.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nationalism, Imperialism and the Balkans'.
questions.a: Discontented Balkan peoples saw their struggles for independent identity as a game of big power rivalry, and this race for expansion ended in the First World War.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nationalism, Imperialism and the Balkans' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Nationalism and Imperialism (source: jess301.txt lines 1160-1210)
